newsitem.title: USA: S.F., Giants reach deal on ballpark lease - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.F., Giants reach deal on ballpark lease - paper.

text.p: The San Francisco Giants baseball team and local elected officials have reached a preliminary deal on a lease for the team's proposed $255 million ballpark, according to a published report on Tuesday.

Under the preliminary agreement on the lease, the city would collect about $1.2 million in rent annually, the San Francisco Chronicle newspaper reported. The team has agreed to an initial 25-year land lease, which could be extended at five-year intervals for a total of 66 years.

San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown told the Board of Supervisors that public costs could total $26 million for preparing the site and making physical improvements around the ballpark, the Chronicle reported.

In September, the Giants said funding of the project would include $140 million from a syndicated bank financing, $100 million in naming rights, sponsorship rights, consession rights and charter seat sales, and $10 to $15 million from a tax increment financing.
